**Test image analysis:**
- Affected part: tomato stem (held between fingers)
- White bleached/rotted area on stem with white cottony mycelium
- Small black sclerotia (hardened fungal bodies) scattered on the white mycelial mat
- Advanced rot causing stem collapse; right side shows dried dead stem tissue

This pattern — white mycelium + black sclerotia on stem — strongly suggests **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**. Let me confirm with one reference image.

The reference shows advanced Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot with whole-plant collapse. The test image shows an earlier/closer stage — the diagnostic white cottony mycelium with embedded black sclerotia directly on the bleached stem tissue, which is the hallmark sign of *Sclerotinia sclerotiorum*.

The match is strong: white mycelium + black sclerotia on a bleached, rotting tomato stem is classic Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot.
